title: The NFL just added insult to injury with Drake Maye's ankle after taking the Patriots out of the ...
description:
The NFL has officially flexed the New England Patriots and Los Angeles Chargers out of Sunday Night Football in Week 12.
The decision comes on the heels of quarterback Drake Maye’s ankle injury Sunday.
The Chargers did just pick up their first win against the Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football this week.
What the flex says about New England’s outlook Moving a game out of Sunday Night Football is the league telling you how it views a matchup.
ET kickoff against a Chargers team coming off its first win, with plenty of questions surrounding the quarterback position.
text:
More news out of New England, and it continues to be bad news. Depending on how you view the rest of this season, you could argue it’s good news. Either way, anyone hoping to see the Patriots under the lights in Week 12 is out of luck.

The NFL has officially flexed the New England Patriots and Los Angeles Chargers out of Sunday Night Football in Week 12. The league is replacing the prime-time matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders and Cleveland Browns, while Patriots-Chargers moves to a 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff.

Drake Maye’s injury is the driving force behind the flex

The timing is no coincidence. The decision comes on the heels of quarterback Drake Maye’s ankle injury Sunday. It’s safe to say this move is due in large part to the Patriots’ struggles, and more specifically, to the injury to their franchise quarterback.

To be fair to the Chargers, Los Angeles isn’t exactly must-watch TV either. The Chargers did just pick up their first win against the Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football this week. Still, that wasn’t going to carry a Sunday night window on its own. Without Maye, New England lost the star power that made this game worthy of a prime-time slot in the first place.

ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported Monday that there is concern within the Patriots organization that Maye fractured his ankle. We will have to wait for updates the team provides from there.

Whether it turns out to be a fracture or a bad sprain, it’s clear that Maye isn’t coming back anytime soon, if at all, during the 2026 season. This decision from the NFL only confirms that.

The Patriots are not the team anyone expected

The truth is, the Maye injury is only the latest crack in a foundation that was already showing plenty of them. The Patriots are not the team anyone expected them to be, and New England has regressed mightily on the defensive side of the football.

The noise away from the field hasn’t helped either. Patriots coach Mike Vrabel has made comments at press conferences about internal player matters. Players have also been sending messages to the NFL. Put it all together, and this is not a clean, well-run operation in New England right now.

Even so, a team can sometimes survive a rough patch on defense and some locker room drama if the quarterback is holding things together. That’s what makes this so damaging. Everything really falls apart when your starting quarterback, the face of your franchise, goes down with an ankle injury.

What the flex says about New England’s outlook

Moving a game out of Sunday Night Football is the league telling you how it views a matchup. For a franchise that had hoped Maye would make it a fixture in prime time, losing a Sunday night showcase stings, especially with the Raiders and Browns taking its place.

Now the Patriots get a 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff against a Chargers team coming off its first win, with plenty of questions surrounding the quarterback position. Until the team provides a clearer update on Maye, the uncertainty in New England isn’t going anywhere, and the NFL has already made its read on the situation.

text:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- The Tennessee Titans placed wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson on injured reserve Tuesday, which will keep him sidelined for at least the next four games.

Robinson suffered an ankle injury late in Tennessee's 40-23 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday.

He has 38 receptions for 272 yards and three touchdowns -- a team high -- this season after signing a four-year, $70 million contract in March to reunite him with offensive coordinator Brian Daboll. Robinson posted back-to-back 90-plus reception seasons in Daboll's offense with the New York Giants in 2024 and 2025.

Robinson's absence comes as the Titans have played the past two games without first-round wide receiver Carnell Tate, who has been out with a shoulder injury. Tate, selected with the No. 4 pick this year, leads the Titans with 413 yards this season on 34 receptions.

Tennessee signed receiver Xavier Restrepo to the active roster from the practice squad in a corresponding move Tuesday. Restrepo got the game-day elevation from the practice squad twice this season. He played 19 snaps after Robinson was injured and caught two passes for 31 yards.

Restrepo signed with the Titans as an undrafted free agent out of Miami in 2025, the same year Tennessee selected Cam Ward with the No. 1 pick.

In one year together at Miami, Ward found Restrepo 69 times for 1,127 yards and 11 touchdowns. Over his five-year career Restrepo finished as Miami's' all-time leader in receptions (200), receiving yards (2,844) and receiving touchdowns (21). He also holds the record for the most 100-yard games in Miami history.

MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- Dolphins defensive tackle Jordan Phillips will miss the rest of the season with torn biceps, a source confirmed Tuesday to ESPN, adding to a string of season-ending injuries Miami has suffered over the past two weeks.

Phillips left Sunday's loss to the Colts in the fourth quarter and did not return. Additional testing this week confirmed his diagnosis, and the team placed Phillips on injured reserve Tuesday.

He is Miami's third defensive tackle to land on season-ending IR in the past two weeks, joining Zach Sieler and Zeek Biggers.

The Dolphins' defensive tackle room is now the thinnest on its team, led by former first-round draft pick Kenneth Grant and Keith Cooper Jr., who was signed from the practice squad last week. Miami also signed defensive lineman Jordan Jefferson to the active roster from the practice squad and added defensive lineman Matthew Butler to the practice squad.

Grant and Cooper finished the game on the field for Miami against the Colts, who completed the quarter with 30 total yards in 13 plays.

"They battled," coach Jeff Hafley said Monday. "In the fourth quarter, I think we had them go three-and-out two or three times to get the ball back to the offense. I give those guys a lot of credit, but it's hard when you're down to two guys there at the end of the game. It's hard with three because those guys rotate so much, taking on the double-teams and all the strain and the effort, so that was tough sledding against a good back yesterday."

The Dolphins selected Phillips in the fifth round in 2025, and he quickly established himself as a rotational defensive lineman, playing 43.4% of their defensive snaps as a rookie. He took on a larger role this season and had played 60% of the team's snaps through nine games.

Phillips, 22, is considered a key part of the NFL's youngest defense, which ranks 10th in yards allowed per game this season. After Sieler's injury in Week 9, Hafley mentioned Phillips as one of the players he expected to step up and lead Miami's defensive line room.

"The way he plays, the way he goes about everything in this building," Hafley said. "I mean, he is a great example of leadership, and whether or not he's a second-year player only, it's going to be his time now to help out those other players."

Beyond the trio of defensive tackles, the Dolphins placed quarterback Malik Willis on IR last week with a groin injury that Hafley said spread to his core. The team is hopeful Willis returns after missing a mandated minimum four games. Hafley said Monday that no surgery is planned for Willis at this time but that the decision is not final.

In other moves Tuesday, the Dolphins signed quarterback Brady Cook and edge rusher Eric Watts to the active roster off the practice squad. Cook will back up interim starter Kyle McCord.

Miami also added several players to the practice squad, including receiver Brady Boyd, defensive linemen Chris Smith and Matthew Butler and kicker Daniel Carlson.

The Dolphins brought in Carlson to replace Zane Gonzalez, who was waived Monday after missing three kicks against the Colts.

text:
The Chicago Bears are likely to be getting a major reinforcement on the offensive side of the ball this week thanks to the return of running back Kyle Monangai.

Monangai has missed each of the last five games becuase of a turf toe injury. It was initially expected that he wouldn't miss more than three games because he wasn't placed on injured reserve, but that ended up not being the case, of course.

Head coach Ben Johnson revealed recently that Monangai did not suffer a setback and it was simply a case of the Bears not knowing exactly how long it would be until Monangai's situation improved.

But none of that matters now. Monangai has taken part in each of the last two practices the Bears have held, including the Monday session out of the bye, and he told reporters after his latest practice that he expects to go in Week 11.

Kyle Monangai's concerning admission

Monangai went into detail about his injury while speaking to the media on Monday and he made a troubling admission.

Monangai said his toe isn't 100% and won't be until the offseason, when he has more time to heal it.

"The time off definitely helped but I mean (the injury is) going to be there," Monangai said. "Offseason I'll heal it. That will be for then."

"It's something I can manage now," Monangai added. "The time off was needed, though, for sure. I feel in a much better spot than I was a month ago."

The obvious concern there is the risk of re-injury, something the Bears can ill-afford given the fact that Monangai has been the team's best running back this season..

A "very painful" injury

Monangai went on to note that the injury is "very painful" for guys at his position in particular, but he was fortunate because he did not come down with the most severe case of turf toe, which is a season-ending issue.

"Yeah, like it's very painful, because especially at my position I'm cutting off (his big toes)," Monangai explained. "And when you're cutting off your insteps you need your big toe to bend and all of these things."

"So you know sometimes guys tear ligaments and that's why you see like some guys get season-ending injuries but some are just a couple weeks," he added. "Luckily I had the blessing of being able to come back. So mine wasn't as extreme. Yeah, it's a painful injury. That's what I'll say."

What is turf toe?

According to the Cleveland Clinic, turf toe is "an injury that affects your big toe joint" and "It happens when your toe remains on the ground and your heel lifts, causing your toe to hyperextend. This motion causes soft tissues and ligaments in your big toe joint to stretch or tear (toe sprain)."

The most extreme cases require surgery, which Monangai clearly didn't need. Lesser turf toe issues get better with rest, ice and medications like ibuprofen or acetaminphen.

Turf toe recovery timelines can be anywhere from as little as a week to several months, depending on the severity. Monangai's issue appears to be around the middle range.

text:
3:39 pm ET November 17, 2026

Goff: Lions 'have to pick up the slack' without Hutchinson

John Niyo

Quarterback Jared Goff is echoing head coach Dan Campbell’s message about the Lions’ response to losing a pair of All-Pro starters on defense in linebacker Jack Campbell and edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson.

“You lose anybody of their caliber, and it's hard to overcome,” Goff said during his weekly radio appearance on 97.1 The Ticket. “But that's what you have the roster for. That's what these guys are here for is to try to fill those voids and pick up the slack. And I know it doesn't come from one guy. It's gonna have to come from a multitude of guys.

“Obviously, you're sick to your stomach about Aidan, but we have no choice move forward and guys have to pick up the slack and that's all of us. That's not just defensively — it's offensively, special teams. So we know the challenges that lie ahead, and we're ready for them.”

2:38 pm ET November 17, 2026

Dan Campbell is not one to sulk about Lions' injuries

John Niyo

ALLEN PARK — Aidan Hutchinson is down, but the Lions aren’t out. And if you expected any moping or pouting from head coach Dan Campbell about his team’s cursed injury luck, well, you must be new here.

Near the end of his Tuesday morning press conference, Campbell was asked about the frustrating reality his team has faced the last three seasons, with a handful of defensive stars taking turns being sidelined with major injuries. And it is jarring when you realize the last time Hutchinson, Alim McNeill, Jack Campbell, Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph all played in a game together was Oct. 13, 2024.

That was the day Hutchinson fractured his tibia and fibula while sacking Dak Prescott in a 47-9 victory in Dallas. That was also 39 games ago, including a playoff loss to Washington that abruptly ended the Lions’ dream season in 2024. And with Hutchinson now facing surgery and another long rehab stint, and Jack Campbell’s prognosis uncertain following a spinal-cord injury suffered this month in a game against Minnesota, that streak will continue indefinitely.

The gloom, however, will not. Not if the Lions' head coach can help it, anyway.

“There's times where if you're not careful, you lay in bed at night and you start thinking about all the what-ifs,” Campbell said, his voice rising in defiance. “And at some point, you just become a miserable piece of s---. And I'm not going to do it. We're not doing it. I refuse to look at it that way.

11:49 am ET November 17, 2026

No timetable yet for Hutchinson's return

John Niyo

ALLEN PARK — Dan Campbell offered another update on Aidan Hutchinson’s injury status Tuesday, Nov. 17, in his first press conference of the week.

“Yeah, it's what it appears to be, unfortunately — ACL — and he will require surgery,” Campbell said. “Obviously, that will knock him out for the season. And knowing Hutch, he will attack this like he did the last time (with a broken leg in 2024), and he will come back better than ever next year.”

Campbell said further testing done after the team returned to Detroit from Germany showed there may be possible meniscus damage in the injured knee as well, which isn’t uncommon with ACL tear.

“Could be, yeah,” Campbell said. “I mean, it sounds like there's a little bit in there. I don't know how significant all of that is. And some of it you're not going to know until you go in there and actually do the procedure.”

It’s unclear when Hutchinson will have surgery to repair his ACL, but Campbell indicated “it'd probably be within the next two weeks here.”

It’s too soon to estimate a recovery timetable. But for comparison’s sake, Alim McNeill, the Lions’ star defensive tackle, suffered a torn ACL in mid-December 2024 and returned to game action 10 months later, though he later admitted he didn’t feel fully recovered until this spring.

9:30 am ET November 17, 2026

Another injury setback for Hutchinson

John Niyo

Two years ago, Aidan Hutchinson’s season was cut short by a broken leg suffered in an early October win in Dallas. Last season, he finished with a career-high 14 ½ sacks, returning to his game-wrecking ways and finishing runner-up to Christian McCaffrey for NFL Comeback Player of the Year.

He talked about that comeback last week in Munich during a Sky Sports interview with former Lions star Ndamukong Suh, saying that injury, when he fractured the tibia and fibia in his left leg while sacking Dallas quarterback Dak Prescott, “offered a new perspective.”

“I mean, one second you go from playing football at the highest level to then, you know, I could barely get up to go to the bathroom by myself,” said Hutchinson, who signed a four-year, $180 million contract extension last October — including $140.5 million in guaranteed money — that is set to kick in next season. “So it really humbles you and it really makes you super grateful for the situation. Every time I leave a game now and I’m healthy, and whatever result happened, ‘I’m just like, ‘Man, I get to play football another day.’”

9:09 am ET November 17, 2026

Lions are better equipped now to deal with Hutchinson's injury

Nolan Bianchi

Aidan Hutchinson, who has six sacks this season, plays the most valuable position on defense and spearheads Detroit’s pass-rushing success because of the attention he commands. But the Lions' defensive front is currently far more equipped to deal with a season-long loss of Hutchinson than it was in 2024, when he broke his leg.

“It’s completely different,” Lions defensive tackle Alim McNeill said after Sunday's game. “We went 15-2 that year, right, when he got hurt? It wasn’t bad. This D-line is a lot different. This defense is a lot different. … We have more pieces that we can plug in to try to get that same — you know, Hutch is Hutch, but we have the pieces … to put in the game to try and create that production. But I think this is a way different D-line, for sure.”

McNeill is in the midst of an All-Pro-caliber campaign, leading the team with 6.5 sacks and seven tackles for a loss while adding 36 pressures and 11 QB hits. Rookie Derrick Moore has come alive in recent weeks, picking up four sacks over his last two games. Edge defender DJ Wonnum (six sacks) is two sacks away from matching a career high. Rookie defensive tackle Skyler Gill-Howard (two sacks) has been one of the best rookie linemen in the league, and Tyleik Williams has quietly put together a really strong campaign rushing the passer, even if he doesn't have the sack numbers to back it up.

8:57 am ET November 17, 2026

Hutchinson's celebration injury is the talk of the NFL

John Niyo

NFL insiders spent much of Monday talking about Aidan Hutchinson's knee injury caused by a leaping celebration of a sack.

On his show, Pat McAfee said, "It's so unlucky, so stupid that this is how our body works. I have no idea how that is a way that your body is allowed to hurt."

ESPN analyst Dan Orlovsky said Monday morning: "If I was a coach, I'm showing this to my players and saying, 'Hey, celebrate. We're not leaving our feet. That one second is not worth it."

Asked Tuesday if he felt he needed to have a conversation with his players about curbing celebrations, Lions coach Dan Campbell said, “No, I don't believe that.”

“I mean, I think what happens speaks for itself, and we're not talking to 8-year-olds here, you know?" said Campbell, a former NFL tight end who finished his playing career in Detroit. "I mean, I'll give you a story. I remember one time I made a big play and I freaking pumped my arm up, and I'm pretty sure I tore my bicep, but I didn't tell anybody. I was just excited. I just pumped my arm. And so, if you say, "Hey, don't pump your arm next time," make sure you stay stoic … man, this game is built off of emotion. And if you have to contain yourself after a play is made — I'm not talking about in the moment in the game, because you got to keep your head — then you're really becoming something you're not."

8:50 am ET November 17, 2026

Hutchinson's injury comes on the heels of Campbell's

John Niyo

Aidan Hutchinson’s torn ACL came just two weeks after middle linebacker Jack Campbell, another All-Pro defensive captain, suffered a spinal-cord injury in a win over Minnesota at Ford Field. Campbell remains hospitalized and the team has said little about his prognosis, though Lions head coach Dan Campbell said Sunday “he's in good spirits and he continues to get better every day.”

After the Lions beat the Patriots in Munich on Sunday, the Lions coach said, “Our guys stepped up and finished, man. We stayed strong. This is the second time this has happened and our guys have responded in a tough situation, didn't bat an eye."

The Lions also were without starting cornerback D.J. Reed in Munich as he missed a second straight game with a hip injury. But Campbell did say Tuesday the plan this week is for former All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph, who has missed more than a year with knee problems, to be activated off the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list this week and return to game action.

8:38 am ET November 17, 2026

Campbell on Hutchinson's injury: 'What a gut punch'

John Niyo

Dan Campbell has confirmed the bad news Lions fans were dreading the last 48 hours: Aidan Hutchinson’s season is over after he suffered a torn ACL in his right knee during Sunday’s win over New England in Munich, Germany.

The All-Pro defensive end, who injured the knee when he landed awkwardly while celebrating a sack of Patriots quarterback Drake Maye, will miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign, dealing a significant blow to the Lions’ Super Bowl hopes.

“Man, what a gut punch,” Campbell said Tuesday, Nov. 17, during his weekly radio spot on 97.1 The Ticket. “He’s such a phenomenal player. This guy's an impact player, but more importantly, he's an unbelievable teammate and he's one of our captains. So it stinks, man. It hits you, and I hate it for him. I hate it for him because he was on a heater, man. What a hell of a year he was having.”

Hutchinson, 26, is the highest-rated edge rusher in the NFL this season, according to Pro Football Focus. He leads the league in quarterback pressures (52) and hurries (34) and is second only to the Raiders’ Maxx Crosby in snaps played (506) at his position. And his mere presence alters opponents gameplans and frees up teammates, as he draws attention — and typically double teams or extra blocking help — on nearly every passing down.

8:33 am ET November 17, 2026

Hutchinson injured while celebrating sack

Richard Silva

With about 10 minutes remaining in the first quarter on Sunday, Nov. 15, in Munich, Germany, Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson sacked Patriots quarterback Drake Maye. Hutchinson then celebrated by leaping into the air. He fell to the ground after landing and grabbed his right leg. Eventually able to stand up and walk to the sideline under his own power, Hutchinson spent a few minutes in the blue medical tent before he made his way to the locker room with trainers at his side. He did not return to the game.

His injury-causing celebration was reminiscent of the season-ending knee injury suffered by Lions linebacker Stephen Tulloch while celebrating a play against the Packers in 2014.

The Lions aren't alone in experiencing celebration injuries. Also in 2014, the Chicago Bears' Lamarr Houston tore an ACL on a jumping sack celebration against the Patriots. Perhaps most famously, Arizona Cardinals kicker Bill Gramatica's leaping, fist-pumping celebration of a 2001 field goal led to a torn ACL on the landing.

The NFL's Week 10 slate delivered plenty of drama. However, several teams left the weekend worrying about something far more important than the final score. Multiple high-profile players suffered potentially significant injuries. Those include franchise quarterbacks, elite pass-catchers, and defensive stars. The most alarming developments came in Munich, where Drake Maye and Aidan Hutchinson were hurt on the same play. Brock Bowers also avoided what initially looked like a devastating ankle injury. Meanwhile, Geno Smith, Drake London and others face uncertain timelines. Here is a closer look at the biggest NFL Week 10 injury developments.

QB Drake Maye, New England Patriots

Patriots fans were left holding their breath during Sunday's 35-10 international loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich. Maye injured his right ankle after being brought down by Hutchinson on an opening-drive sack and did not return. New England reportedly fears the quarterback may have suffered an ankle fracture that could end his season. Further evaluation is necessary before a definitive diagnosis or recovery timeline can be established.

The Patriots enter their Week 11 bye at 5-5, giving the organization additional time to assess its options. If Maye is sidelined, Tommy DeVito is the quarterback who finished Sunday's game and would be the leading candidate to take over. Wide receiver SJ Brown also aggravated a hamstring injury against Detroit, adding another concern to New England's offense.

DE Aidan Hutchinson, Detroit Lions

Detroit's dominant victory came at a devastating cost. Hutchinson suffered a torn right ACL while celebrating a third-down sack of Maye. Hutchinson is expected to miss the remainder of the season. Further testing is also being conducted to determine whether additional knee damage occurred.

Losing Hutchinson is an enormous blow to the Lions defense. He recorded his sixth sack of the season before going down. Kelvin Sheppard will now have to find new ways to generate consistent pressure.

TE Brock Bowers, Las Vegas Raiders

Bowers' ankle injury was another major concern after the Raiders' 21-13 home loss to Seattle. The star tight end was hurt during the opening drive. He briefly returned after receiving treatment. However, he eventually left the contest for good. Fortunately, Monday brought encouraging news. Head coach Klint Kubiak said it was not as bad as initially feared. They have listed Bowers as day-to-day while further evaluations continue.

That is a major relief for Las Vegas. Bowers leads the Raiders in receiving and remains a central piece of the passing attack. Any absence would place additional pressure on Michael Mayer and the team's other receiving options, particularly with the offense trying to develop consistency.

QB Geno Smith, New York Jets

The Jets' frustrating 2026 campaign took another hit during Sunday's 31-12 loss to Buffalo. Smith initially underwent a concussion evaluation after taking a hit. He did clear the assessment and return to the game. Unfortunately, he subsequently suffered an ankle injury and was ruled out.

Smith avoided leaving the stadium in a walking boot. Still, that alone does not establish the severity of the injury. Further evaluation will determine whether he can return for Week 11. With New York sitting at 2-8, the coaching staff has little reason to rush its starting quarterback back prematurely. Cade Klubnik stepped in after Smith exited. Wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. also aggravated an ankle injury and did not return.

WR Drake London, Atlanta Falcons

Atlanta's 35-13 loss to Kansas City also came with a worrying development. London sustained a possible concussion. He was evaluated during the contest. His availability will depend on the results of further assessments and whether he enters or progresses through the NFL's concussion protocol.

At 3-7, the Falcons can ill afford to lose their leading perimeter threat. If London cannot return promptly, Atlanta will need Kyle Pitts Sr. and its remaining receivers to shoulder more of the passing-game responsibility.

RB Woody Marks, Houston Texans

Houston's backfield situation also deserves attention after Sunday's 27-24 loss to Cleveland. Marks exited with a knee injury, not a concussion as initially reported. The Texans' official Week 10 injury report listed him with a knee issue. He had been able to participate in practice before the game.

With Houston scheduled for Thursday night football in Week 11, the short turnaround makes his availability worth monitoring. David Montgomery and the team's other backfield options could be asked to shoulder additional work if Marks cannot go.

WR Jordan Addison, Minnesota Vikings

Addison missed Minnesota's 30-10 divisional victory over Green Bay after injuring his thumb during Friday's practice. He was ruled out for the matchup. His return will depend on how the injury responds and whether he can safely catch passes.

Justin Jefferson and the Vikings' remaining receiving options handled the workload against Green Bay. Of course, getting Addison back would give the passing attack another important dimension.

Other notable Week 10 injuries

Several other teams are monitoring important players. Pittsburgh guard Mason McCormick suffered an ankle injury, while safety DeShon Elliott was ruled out with a knee issue. Kansas City guard Trey Smith exited with a concussion. Seattle lost running back George Holani (knee) and right tackle Abraham Lucas (ankle). Indianapolis tackle Bernhard Raimann was ruled out after a concussion evaluation. Cincinnati guard Dalton Risner was listed with an illness rather than a knee injury.

Week 10 was a costly reminder of how quickly injuries can reshape a season. The coming days of evaluations and practice reports will determine which teams face extended absences and which stars might return sooner than expected.

title: 'Gut punch' for Lions as Aidan Hutchinson is out for season - The Detroit News
description:

It’s unclear when Hutchinson will have surgery to repair his ACL, and it’s too soon to estimate a recovery timetable.
And that was just one in a series of major injuries that eventually derailed what appeared to be a dream season for the Lions.
They lost a half-dozen defensive starters in all, and though it didn’t stop Campbell’s team from rolling to a franchise-best 15-2 regular-season record and a second straight NFC North title, the Lions’ season ended abruptly with divisional playoff loss at home to Washington.
text:
DETROIT — Dan Campbell confirmed the bad news Lions fans were dreading the last 48 hours: Aidan Hutchinson’s season is over after he suffered a torn ACL in his right knee during a win over the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany, on Sunday, Nov. 15.

The All-Pro defensive end, who injured the knee when he landed awkwardly while celebrating a sack of Patriots quarterback Drake Maye, will miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign, dealing a significant blow to the Lions’ Super Bowl hopes.

“Man, what a gut punch,” Campbell said Tuesday, Nov. 17, during his weekly radio spot on 97.1 The Ticket. “He’s such a phenomenal player. This guy's an impact player, but more importantly, he's an unbelievable teammate and he's one of our captains. So it stinks, man. It hits you, and I hate it for him. I hate it for him because he was on a heater, man. What a hell of a year he was having.”

Hutchinson, 26, is the highest-rated edge rusher in the NFL this season, according to Pro Football Focus. He leads the league in quarterback pressures (52) and hurries (34) and is second only to the Raiders’ Maxx Crosby in snaps played (506) at his position. And his mere presence alters opponents gameplans and frees up teammates, as he draws attention — and typically double teams or extra blocking help — on nearly every passing down.

At a news conference later Tuesday, Campbell said further testing done after the team returned to Detroit from Germany showed there may be possible meniscus damage in the injured knee as well. It’s unclear when Hutchinson will have surgery to repair his ACL, and it’s too soon to estimate a recovery timetable. Alim McNeill, the Lions’ star defensive tackle, suffered a torn ACL in mid-December 2024 and returned to game action 10 months later, though he later admitted he didn’t feel fully recovered until this spring.

Replacing Hutchinson's production will be a daunting task for the Lions, who are riding a five-game win streak and sit atop the NFC North with a 7-2 record. Detroit ranks third in the NFL in sacks (32) and fifth in rushing defense through nine games. Rookie Derrick Moore, who played a season-high 40 snaps Sunday after Hutchinson’s early exit, is expected to replace him as a starter opposite DJ Wonnum.

Moore’s play of late has been encouraging: He was credited with four pressures and two sacks Sunday against New England, becoming only the second rookie in franchise history (Ziggy Ansah, 2013) to post consecutive multiple-sack games. But as Campbell reiterated Tuesday, he’ll need more from everyone now.

“Now, what has to happen?" Campbell said. "What can happen, and what will happen, is that somebody's got to pick up the the slack. Somebody has to fill that void, and it's not going to be one person. One person is not going to fill the void of of Aidan Hutchinson.”

Still, the concern for the Lions now is the compounding effect of injuries on a defense that has shown dramatic improvement after a brutal start to this season.

Hutchinson’s torn ACL came just two weeks after middle linebacker Jack Campbell, another All-Pro defensive captain, suffered a spinal-cord injury in a win over Minnesota at Ford Field. Campbell remains hospitalized and the team has said little about his prognosis, though the Lions’ head coach said Sunday “he's in good spirits and he continues to get better every day.”

The Lions also were without starting cornerback D.J. Reed in Munich as he missed a second straight game with a hip injury. But Dan Campbell did say Tuesday the plan this week is for former All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph, who has missed more than a year with knee problems, to be activated off the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list this week and return to game action.

“Yeah, I mean, barring anything else here negatively, which there hasn't been any — he's progressed nicely here — the plan would be to get him going this week,” Campbell said. “Get him going, and get him into Tampa Bay, let him play.”

Two years ago, Hutchinson’s season was cut short by a broken leg suffered in an early October win in Dallas. And that was just one in a series of major injuries that eventually derailed what appeared to be a dream season for the Lions. They lost a half-dozen defensive starters in all, and though it didn’t stop Campbell’s team from rolling to a franchise-best 15-2 regular-season record and a second straight NFC North title, the Lions’ season ended abruptly with divisional playoff loss at home to Washington.

“All hands on deck,” Dan Campbell said. “No different than (what) we did with Jack. No different than what we did in ’24. I mean, the bottom line is this: we're prepared to handle this storm. We are suited to handle this storm actually, I think, better than we were in 24. That that's the good news."

For Hutchinson, however, it's another major injury setback. The former No. 2 overall pick out of Michigan ranks sixth in sacks since he entered the league in 2022, racking up 49 in 65 games. Last season, he finished with a career-high 14 ½ sacks, returning to his game-wrecking ways and finishing runner-up to Christian McCaffrey for NFL Comeback Player of the Year.

He talked about that comeback last week in Munich during a Sky Sports interview with former Lions star Ndamukong Suh, saying that injury, when he fractured the tibia and fibia in his left leg while sacking Dallas quarterback Dak Prescott, “offered a new perspective.”

“I mean, one second you go from playing football at the highest level to then, you know, I could barely get up to go to the bathroom by myself,” said Hutchinson, who signed a four-year, $180 million contract extension last October — including $140.5 million in guaranteed money — that is set to kick in next season. “So it really humbles you and it really makes you super grateful for the situation. Every time I leave a game now and I’m healthy, and whatever result happened, ‘I’m just like, ‘Man, I get to play football another day.’”

Sunday, he left the field under his own power. But the concern on his face was obvious after Hutchinson had leaped into the air to celebrate a first-quarter sack and then immediately fell to the turf grabbing at his knee. It was a scene eerily reminiscent of a similar sack celebration by former Lions linebacker Stephen Tulloch back in 2014, when he also tore his ACL.

Asked if he felt he needed to have a conversation with his players about curbing celebrations, Campbell said, “No, I don't believe that.”

“I mean, I think what happens speaks for itself, and we're not talking to 8-year-olds here, you know?" said Campbell, a former NFL tight end who finished his playing career in Detroit. "I mean, I'll give you a story. I remember one time I made a big play and I freaking pumped my arm up, and I'm pretty sure I tore my bicep, but I didn't tell anybody. I was just excited. I just pumped my arm. And so, if you say, "Hey, don't pump your arm next time," make sure you stay stoic … man, this game is built off of emotion. And if you have to contain yourself after a play is made — I'm not talking about in the moment in the game, because you got to keep your head — then you're really becoming something you're not.

“So, look, it's one of those things that happened. I hate it. I know he hates it, but I mean the number of moves that I've seen Hutch make — and the number of plyometrics, explosive movements, the spins, the one-leg lateral movements, lateral bounds, bounces — I'm just like it was one of those things, man. I hate it, but no, I think we all understand what it is, and let's be smart. But no, I'm not going to say nobody celebrates anymore.”

description:

Patriots injury analysis: NFL Week 10 QB Drake Maye: While all eyes were on the Lions’ Aidan Hutchinson, who was down on the field after tearing his ACL while celebrating, Maye himself also hobbled off the field after the third-down sack that ended the game’s opening drive.

text:
Sunday was a bad day for the New England Patriots. Besides losing their Week 10 game against the Detroit Lions with a final score of 35-10, they also saw their starting quarterback go down with what appears to be a significant ankle injury.

Drake Maye was not the only Patriot to leave Munich’s Allianz Arena as an injury concern. After rewatching the game, here is the full list of players to get banged up during the game. Brace yourselves, it’s a long one.

Patriots injury analysis: NFL Week 10

QB Drake Maye: While all eyes were on the Lions’ Aidan Hutchinson, who was down on the field after tearing his ACL while celebrating, Maye himself also hobbled off the field after the third-down sack that ended the game’s opening drive. He consulted with head coach Mike Vrabel, received some further treatment while sitting on the bench for a while, and then headed into the blue medical tent on the sideline. From there, while Tommy DeVito was getting ready to go in, it was off to the locker room. Maye was initially announced as questionable to return because of an ankle injury, and ruled out midway through the second quarter ruled out entirely. The timing of that announcement was conspicuous: normally, those downgrades only happen at the half, which in turn gave a first hint at the injury’s severity.

LT Will Campbell: Before Drake Maye visited the medical tent, another player did. Left tackle Will Campbell briefly went in after the game’s first drive. He departed and returned to the sideline, and no injury was announced. Campbell ended up playing 53 snaps and was only pulled after Lan Larison’s fourth-quarter touchdown, when the score was way out of hand.

RT Morgan Moses: The Patriots’ first drive of the game ended in disaster, and the second didn’t start much better. On the first snap, right tackle Morgan Moses remained on the ground after getting rolled up from behind. He received medical attention on the field, hobbled off, and eventually departed for the locker room. Initially announced as questionable to return, he returned to the sideline in the second quarter to try out his knee. Shortly thereafter, he was back on the field and remained there until after the aforementioned Lan Larison score.

S Craig Woodson: Woodson was nowhere to be seen as the Patriots began their third defensive series in the early second quarter. Why? Because he too was in the medical tent. No injury was announced, however, and he returned after missing one three-snap series.

LB Robert Spillane: Spillane required medical attention late in the second quarter after he seemingly collided with Kevin Byard’s knee as the safety was catching an interception in the end zone. He took off his helmet in pain, and accompanied by members of the medical staff and head coach Mike Vrabel slowly walked off the field. He did return at the start of the second half but ultimately left the contest again midway through the third quarter due to what the team announced as an illness.

CB Charles Woods: Woods, who started the game as an injury replacement for Carlton Davis (knee), remained on the ground after Amon-Ra St. Brown’s catch-and-run touchdown in the third quarter. He came down after trying to keep St. Brown out of the end zone, with Robert Spillane — for whom that also was the final snap of the game — providing the final impetus. Woods limped off the field and into the locker room, but the Patriots never announced any injury.

WR A.J. Brown: In his first game back from a knee injury, Brown had to walk off the field with trainers after his first catch, a 6-yarder in the third quarter; his head had come down hard on the play prompting him to be removed from the game. He sat out two snaps before returning, promptly caught a 21-yard pass, and was injured again. This time, there was no coming back: after a brief stint in the blue medical tent, he walked to the locker room and was announced as questionable to return with a hamstring injury. A short time later, he was ruled out.

ED Dre’Mont Jones: According to FOX sideline reporter Pam Oliver, Jones was “in absolute agony” at one point in the fourth quarter. Eventually, the team announced him as questionable to return due to cramps. His final snap of the day had come with 4:23 in the third period, although he suffered no obvious injury on that play.

What this means for the Patriots

There is no sugar-coating it: this is the worst-case scenario.

Drake Maye is the Patriots’ most important player, and initial reports suggest that he might have suffered a fractured ankle — the same injury that also knocked starting right guard Mike Onwenu out in Week 2. If that diagnosis is confirmed, Maye missing the rest of the season is the likeliest outcome.

The ramifications of that would be massive, as we have discussed here in greater detail. The most immediate outcome, however, would be Tommy DeVito taking over as starting quarterback for most if not all of the remaining season while the eighth-seeded Patriots, against all odds, will try to get back into the playoff picture.

If Maye’s injury situation wasn’t enough, the Patriots are also facing questions elsewhere.

A total of seven other players received medical attention at some point, including six regular starters and a key reserve. The most concerning of those are the four players who did not finish the game: Robert Spillane, Charles Woods, A.J. Brown and Dre’Mont Jones. Brown in particular stands out among them, as he declined to speak to the media afterwards and left the locker room with a notable limp.

For the 29-year-old offseason trade pickup, this is a continuation of what has been a disappointing season so far — something that can be said for the Patriots and their injury situation as a whole.

They are headed into a much-needed bye week now, but questions will remain. None is bigger than Drake Maye’s outlook, of course, but as the list above shows he is only the tip of the proverbial iceberg.

text:
Lions star defensive end Aidan Hutchinson joined an exclusive but undesirable club of NFL players who have suffered a serious injury while celebrating.

After sacking New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye in the first quarter Sunday, Nov. 15, in Munich, Germany, Hutchinson leaped into the air, then immediately fell to the turf grabbing at his right knee after he landed. He will miss the rest of the season with a torn ACL. It was a scene eerily reminiscent of a similar sack celebration by former Lions linebacker Stephen Tulloch in 2014, when he also tore his ACL.

The Lions aren't alone in experiencing celebration injuries. Also in 2014, the Chicago Bears linebacker Lamarr Houston tore an ACL after a jumping sack celebration against the Patriots. Perhaps most famously, Arizona Cardinals kicker Bill Gramatica's leaping, fist-pumping celebration of a 2001 field goal led to a torn ACL on the landing. Washington quarterback Gus Frerotte ended up in the hospital with a sprained neck in 1997 after head-butting a padded wall after scoring a touchdown.

ESPN analyst Dan Orlovsky said of Hutchinson's injury on Monday: "If I was a coach, I'm showing this to my players and saying, 'Hey, celebrate. We're not leaving our feet. That one second is not worth it."

But asked Tuesday if he felt he needed to have a conversation with his players about curbing celebrations, Lions head coach Dan Campbell said, “No, I don't believe that.”

“I mean, I think what happens speaks for itself, and we're not talking to 8-year-olds here, you know?" said Campbell, a former NFL tight end who finished his playing career in Detroit.

Then he shared his own story of a celebration-related injury. "I remember one time I made a big play and I freaking pumped my arm up, and I'm pretty sure I tore my bicep, but I didn't tell anybody," he said. "I was just excited. I just pumped my arm. And so, if you say, 'Hey, don't pump your arm next time, make sure you stay stoic' … man, this game is built off of emotion. And if you have to contain yourself after a play is made — I'm not talking about in the moment in the game, because you got to keep your head — then you're really becoming something you're not."

“So, look, it's one of those things that happened. I hate it. I know he hates it, but I mean the number of moves that I've seen Hutch make — and the number of plyometrics, explosive movements, the spins, the one-leg lateral movements, lateral bounds, bounces — I'm just like it was one of those things, man. I hate it, but no, I think we all understand what it is, and let's be smart. But no, I'm not going to say nobody celebrates anymore.”

title: Bills' Week 11 Injury Outlook: Updates on Christian Benford, Dee Alford, Five Others
description:
Both starting outside cornerback Christian Benford and slot cornerback Dee Alford did not finish the game due to in-game injuries.
In a positive development, starting right tackle Spencer Brown was active despite being doubtful due to an ankle injury.
The Bills have a normal Sunday-to-Sunday game week ahead with the Miami Dolphins set to visit on November 22.

text:
The Buffalo Bills' defensive backfield suffered its share of bumps and bruises during the November 15 road win over the New York Jets.

Both starting outside cornerback Christian Benford and slot cornerback Dee Alford did not finish the game due to in-game injuries. Starting inside linebacker Dorian Williams saw his day end early in the fourth quarter.

Starting safeties Cole Bishop and Amani Hooker, along with cornerback Maxwell Hairston, all briefly received medical attention during the Week 10 matinee, but all returned to action before the day was done. The same can be said for wide receiver Keon Coleman.

In a positive development, starting right tackle Spencer Brown was active despite being doubtful due to an ankle injury. Brown played the entire game up until the final three kneel-downs, and he appears ready to keep rolling.

The Bills have a normal Sunday-to-Sunday game week ahead with the Miami Dolphins set to visit on November 22. Only four days after that, however, they'll host the Kansas City Chiefs for a Thanksgiving night matchup.

"We're at the point in the season where the reality [is] Wednesday is going to be just a walkthrough. There's accumulation of reps and practices," said head coach Joe Brady on Monday afternoon.

Here are the injured players who warrant monitoring as the practice week progresses.

CB Dee Alford

Alford initially left for a few plays late in the second quarter. He was evaluated for a head injury and cleared to return.

Back on the field for the Jets' opening drive of the second half, Alford went down to the ground hard in the end zone while covering wide receiver Garrett Wilson on a 1st-and-goal play. He left for another concussion check, and the Bills subsequently ruled him out for the remainder of the game.

CB Christian Benford

Benford was questionable entering the game with a wrist injury from the November 9 primetime win, but he appeared unaffected in the early going.

Injuring his groin during the second half, Benford was ruled out and missed 18 of 71 reps. It doesn't sound as if he'll be ready to practice by Wednesday, but that doesn't mean he won't play Sunday.

"I've said all along, there's guys that might not practice, but have played a lot of football for us, and, if they have the opportunity to go play in the game, we're going to play them. Christian's really no different, and we'll kind of just progress it day by day," said Brady.

S Cole Bishop

Late in the fourth quarter, Bishop appeared to get banged up while diving toward Jets' running back Braelon Allen on a screen play. He was shown be examined on the sideline, missing only three total snaps.

"A little sore, shoulder hurts a little bit, but we'll see how we're feeling tomorrow. [I'm] sure, we'll be alright, though," said Bishop postgame (h/t WGR's Sal Capaccio for the audio).

WR Keon Coleman

Early in the fourth quarter, Coleman absorbed a helmet-to-helmet hit from Jets' safety Minkah Fitzpatrick while making a catch along the Bills' sideline. After being evaluated for a head injury, the independent party cleared Coleman to return. He was back in action with 9:59 remaining in the game.

CB Maxwell Hairston

Injured on a first down with under 3:00 remaining in the game, Hairston exited briefly with what's presumed to be an ankle issue. He returned after an injury timeout.

S Amani Hooker

Hooker was spotted entering the medical tent, but it didn't cause him to miss a single rep. He was the Bills' lone defender to play 100 percent of snaps.

LB Dorian Williams

Williams was ruled questionable to return due to a calf problem early in fourth quarter, but fourth-round rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr took over for him the rest of the way. His last play came with 2:07 remaining in the third quarter.

title: NFL Week 10 injury roundup: Drake Maye, Brock Bowers and more - ClutchPoints
description:
Brock Bowers also avoided what initially looked like a devastating ankle injury.
Here is a closer look at the biggest NFL Week 10 injury developments.
TE Brock Bowers, Las Vegas Raiders Bowers' ankle injury was another major concern after the Raiders' 21-13 home loss to Seattle.
Pittsburgh guard Mason McCormick suffered an ankle injury, while safety DeShon Elliott was ruled out with a knee issue.
Cincinnati guard Dalton Risner was listed with an illness rather than a knee injury.
text:
The NFL's Week 10 slate delivered plenty of drama. However, several teams left the weekend worrying about something far more important than the final score. Multiple high-profile players suffered potentially significant injuries. Those include franchise quarterbacks, elite pass-catchers, and defensive stars. The most alarming developments came in Munich, where Drake Maye and Aidan Hutchinson were hurt on the same play. Brock Bowers also avoided what initially looked like a devastating ankle injury. Meanwhile, Geno Smith, Drake London and others face uncertain timelines. Here is a closer look at the biggest NFL Week 10 injury developments.

QB Drake Maye, New England Patriots

Patriots fans were left holding their breath during Sunday's 35-10 international loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich. Maye injured his right ankle after being brought down by Hutchinson on an opening-drive sack and did not return. New England reportedly fears the quarterback may have suffered an ankle fracture that could end his season. Further evaluation is necessary before a definitive diagnosis or recovery timeline can be established.

The Patriots enter their Week 11 bye at 5-5, giving the organization additional time to assess its options. If Maye is sidelined, Tommy DeVito is the quarterback who finished Sunday's game and would be the leading candidate to take over. Wide receiver SJ Brown also aggravated a hamstring injury against Detroit, adding another concern to New England's offense.

DE Aidan Hutchinson, Detroit Lions

Detroit's dominant victory came at a devastating cost. Hutchinson suffered a torn right ACL while celebrating a third-down sack of Maye. Hutchinson is expected to miss the remainder of the season. Further testing is also being conducted to determine whether additional knee damage occurred.

Losing Hutchinson is an enormous blow to the Lions defense. He recorded his sixth sack of the season before going down. Kelvin Sheppard will now have to find new ways to generate consistent pressure.

TE Brock Bowers, Las Vegas Raiders

Bowers' ankle injury was another major concern after the Raiders' 21-13 home loss to Seattle. The star tight end was hurt during the opening drive. He briefly returned after receiving treatment. However, he eventually left the contest for good. Fortunately, Monday brought encouraging news. Head coach Klint Kubiak said it was not as bad as initially feared. They have listed Bowers as day-to-day while further evaluations continue.

That is a major relief for Las Vegas. Bowers leads the Raiders in receiving and remains a central piece of the passing attack. Any absence would place additional pressure on Michael Mayer and the team's other receiving options, particularly with the offense trying to develop consistency.

QB Geno Smith, New York Jets

The Jets' frustrating 2026 campaign took another hit during Sunday's 31-12 loss to Buffalo. Smith initially underwent a concussion evaluation after taking a hit. He did clear the assessment and return to the game. Unfortunately, he subsequently suffered an ankle injury and was ruled out.

Smith avoided leaving the stadium in a walking boot. Still, that alone does not establish the severity of the injury. Further evaluation will determine whether he can return for Week 11. With New York sitting at 2-8, the coaching staff has little reason to rush its starting quarterback back prematurely. Cade Klubnik stepped in after Smith exited. Wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. also aggravated an ankle injury and did not return.

WR Drake London, Atlanta Falcons

Atlanta's 35-13 loss to Kansas City also came with a worrying development. London sustained a possible concussion. He was evaluated during the contest. His availability will depend on the results of further assessments and whether he enters or progresses through the NFL's concussion protocol.

At 3-7, the Falcons can ill afford to lose their leading perimeter threat. If London cannot return promptly, Atlanta will need Kyle Pitts Sr. and its remaining receivers to shoulder more of the passing-game responsibility.

RB Woody Marks, Houston Texans

Houston's backfield situation also deserves attention after Sunday's 27-24 loss to Cleveland. Marks exited with a knee injury, not a concussion as initially reported. The Texans' official Week 10 injury report listed him with a knee issue. He had been able to participate in practice before the game.

With Houston scheduled for Thursday night football in Week 11, the short turnaround makes his availability worth monitoring. David Montgomery and the team's other backfield options could be asked to shoulder additional work if Marks cannot go.

WR Jordan Addison, Minnesota Vikings

Addison missed Minnesota's 30-10 divisional victory over Green Bay after injuring his thumb during Friday's practice. He was ruled out for the matchup. His return will depend on how the injury responds and whether he can safely catch passes.

Justin Jefferson and the Vikings' remaining receiving options handled the workload against Green Bay. Of course, getting Addison back would give the passing attack another important dimension.

Other notable Week 10 injuries

Several other teams are monitoring important players. Pittsburgh guard Mason McCormick suffered an ankle injury, while safety DeShon Elliott was ruled out with a knee issue. Kansas City guard Trey Smith exited with a concussion. Seattle lost running back George Holani (knee) and right tackle Abraham Lucas (ankle). Indianapolis tackle Bernhard Raimann was ruled out after a concussion evaluation. Cincinnati guard Dalton Risner was listed with an illness rather than a knee injury.

I hate to knock the Lions down after a convincing win over the Patriots, but losing Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson may be a bridge too far for this team to recover from. I think the Lions are still good enough to limp into the playoffs, but can this offense score at a historic rate to make up for all the attrition?

Non-QB MVP at midseason: RB Jahmyr Gibbs

There’s a reason the Lions made Gibbs the NFL’s highest-paid running back over the offseason. And he has proved to be worth every penny after a phenomenal start to his fourth season as the team’s clear lead back. With 62 career touchdowns, the 24-year-old recently passed Hall of Famer Terrell Davis (61) for the most through a player’s first four seasons in NFL history, per ESPN Research. His 1,384 scrimmage yards are the most a Lions player has produced through the first nine games of any season, and he has already scored 13 touchdowns.

The Lions’ season changed with the reported ACL injury to defensive end Aidan Hutchinson. They were already without linebacker Jack Campbell, arguably the second-best player on the defense, and Detroit lost its unquestioned star because of a sack celebration. That’s brutal. Derrick Moore and DJ Wonnum are capable vets and will fill in, but they’re nowhere near Hutchinson’s level.

“Any time you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is — he’s a captain of ours — that doesn’t make things easy,” Lions head coach Dan Campbell said, according to NFL.com.

The Lions won on Sunday without Hutchinson for most of the game to improve to 7-2, and perhaps they have enough wins banked to make the playoffs in what will be a difficult wild-card race. But their hopes of being a Super Bowl contender are likely dashed without their two best defensive players.

title: Mason McCormick's injury will test Steelers' biggest strength: Their offensive line - NFL.com
description:
Pittsburgh built an identity and rode a four-game winning streak heading into Sunday night thanks in large part to their young and developing offensive line.
At a position group in which continuity and chemistry are critical, the Steelers' offensive line will be tested to maintain that high level of play without one of the players most responsible for its success.
But the personality of the offensive line and the heartbeat flowed through the two trash-talking guards.
Drafted in the seventh round in 2023, Anderson has exceeded his draft position and proven to be a malleable piece of the offensive line.

text:
The medical staff rushed onto the field Sunday in Cincinnati as Mason McCormick writhed in pain on the turf. The severity of the injury and the way the Pittsburgh Steelers' feel about their starting left guard were clear from the player's reaction. As the doctors and trainers fastened an air cast to McCormick's right ankle and prepared to cart him off the field, teammates gathered around on a knee. Emotions flowed.

"It made a lot of us sick to our stomach," tackle Troy Fautanu said. "I've never seen anything like that before."

During the 38-18 blowout, the Bengals exposed the weaknesses on the Steelers' roster, particularly Pittsburgh's defensive backs and injury-marred receiving corps. As the Steelers look to move past the letdown, they will now be challenged to maintain their strength in the trenches without a key cog.

Pittsburgh built an identity and rode a four-game winning streak heading into Sunday night thanks in large part to their young and developing offensive line. From Weeks 5 through 8, only one team accumulated more rushing yards than Pittsburgh's 564, and only two had a better yard per carry average than the Steelers' 5.3. At a position group in which continuity and chemistry are critical, the Steelers' offensive line will be tested to maintain that high level of play without one of the players most responsible for its success.

"It's definitely a time to rally around it, because that was definitely a dynamic of this football team that we all want, especially me," Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said. "I believe it starts in the trenches. I think the tradition, the history of the Steelers reflects that.

"We'll continue to go down that road, but it's time for others to step up. This is how every season goes. Unfortunately, you have injuries, and it's opportunity for others. But it's also an opportunity for us to make sure we're utilizing all of our resources."

The Steelers' most significant investments up front may have come at tackle, with a pair of first-round picks in Fautanu and Max Iheanachor, and at center with second-round selection Zach Frazier. But the personality of the offensive line and the heartbeat flowed through the two trash-talking guards. Thrust into a starting role in the middle of his rookie season, McCormick has consistently improved to become a mauling run blocker, reliable pass protector and excellent communicator.

"I'll just tell you from my perspective, Mason is clearly one of the leaders on the team," McCarthy said, adding that McCormick is on the team's leadership council.

Fautanu has often said there's no one else he'd rather play alongside. Now, he has no choice in the matter. On Monday, McCarthy acknowledged that McCormick sustained a significant injury but did not have a definitive timeline. If the Steelers are going to maintain their playoff position and make some noise in December and January, they'll need to weather this injury.

Versatile lineman Spencer Anderson appears to be the next man up. Drafted in the seventh round in 2023, Anderson has exceeded his draft position and proven to be a malleable piece of the offensive line. Over the years, he's contributed at tackle, guard and as the sixth offensive lineman in jumbo packages.

"Spencer's just a 360 football player in my view," McCarthy said. "Just coming in here to see to see him play in different positions… He's a gifted football player. This will be his opportunity."

Where the starting left guard position goes from here will hinge upon a number of factors, including McCormick's recovery timeline, Anderson's performance and the readiness of rookie third-round pick Gennings Dunker, who is one of the x-factors.

At the University of Iowa, Dunker was arguably the most consistent lineman from a group that won the Joe Moore Award as the top offensive line in college football. The Hawkeyes' run-heavy style of play was reflected in Dunker's performance early in camp. His tape told two stories. As a run blocker, Dunker is already an old-school mauler, using his tree-trunk legs to punish defenders. However, he still needed considerable refinement as a pass protector, especially as he makes the transition from college tackle to NFL guard. McCarthy said that Dunker is "definitely part of the conversation" as the Steelers consider different possibilities.

Whether it's Anderson, Dunker or some combination of the two, the Steelers will need to continue to lean on the men up front, even with one of the most important pieces missing. How well they handle the injury will play a major role in determing where the season goes from here.

text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers returned from their quiet bye weekend with a flurry of roster moves on Sunday, including two involving the quarterback position. Easton Stick was promoted from the practice squad to the active roster and the team then filled that spot on the practice squad by signing Cooper Rush.

In addition, the Buccaneers signed wide receiver David Sills to the practice squad, releasing cornerback Brandon Johnson to make room on that 17-man unit.

The quarterback maneuvers lend credence to the reports that surfaced on Sunday indicating that starting quarterback Baker Mayfield is dealing with a lower-leg injury. If Mayfield is unable to play on Sunday in Detroit, rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels would draw his fourth start of the season with Stick serving as his backup.

Stick was previously active for each of Daniels' three starts in Weeks 4-6 as Mayfield was recovering from a dislocated right thumb. In each of those three weeks, however, he was elevated from the practice squad to be eligible for the game, and that is the maximum number of practice squad elevations per player during the regular season.

Stick was signed to the Buccaneers' practice squad on August 31 but he has prior experience in Offensive Coordinator Zac Robinson's system, as the two were together last season with the Atlanta Falcons. A fifth-round pick by the Los Angeles Chargers in 2019, Stick has appeared in a total of six games with four starts, completing 111 of 174 passes (63.8%) for 1,129 yards, three touchdowns, one interception and an 85.7 passer rating.

Rush also has NFL starting experience, having opened 18 games with Dallas, Baltimore and Atlanta. That includes two starts for the Falcons this season, as he joined Atlanta near the end of July and started the first two games of the regular season before being released on October 19. In all, Rush has played in 44 games and has completed 386 of 635 passes (60.8%) for 3,995 yards, 21 touchdowns and 18 interceptions. His most extensive playing time came with the Cowboys in 2024, when he started eight games and compiled a 4-4 record while throwing 12 touchdown passes against five interceptions. Rush initially entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent out of Central Michigan with the Cowboys in 2017.

Sills was on the Buccaneers' active roster for three weeks before being waived on November 10, which created the roster spot now used for Stick's promotion. He started the season on injured reserve but was activated on October 22 and played in three games, though without drawing a target in the pass game. Tampa Bay signed Sills as a free agent in April, also reuniting him with Robinson, who had also been his coordinator in Atlanta in 2025 when he put up a career-best 18 catches for 191 yards and two touchdowns. He has also played for the New York Giants and Denver Broncos, and in 33 career games (11 starts), he has recorded 31 receptions for 314 yards and two scores.

Johnson was on the Buccaneers' practice squad for five weeks. He previously saw regular season action with the Philadelphia Eagles in 2025, appearing three games with one start.

title: Aidan Hutchinson Is To Blame For Freak Injury, Must Tone Down Celebrations
description:
The Detroit Lions continued their winning ways Sunday morning in Munich, Germany, easily defeating the New England Patriots, 35-10, for their fifth straight win.
Yet, the Week 10 victory was overshadowed by the likely season-ending knee injury to EDGE Aidan Hutchinson, the Lions’ star pass-rusher.
His sack of Maye was his seventh on the season, and he also logged another two pressures in the international affair, bringing his season total to 52 (the second-highest total in the NFL).
I'm fully aware that players like Hutchinson are also entertainers and that they have a genuine passion and love for playing the game.
He needs to be steadfast with it and emphasize there is no wiggle room for a Hutchinson 2.0.
text:
The Detroit Lions continued their winning ways Sunday morning in Munich, Germany, easily defeating the New England Patriots, 35-10, for their fifth straight win.

It was a dominant effort from start to finish for Dan Campbell's team, which accumulated nearly 500 total yards (494) and allowed just 151 yards to Mike Vrabel's squad.

Yet, the Week 10 victory was overshadowed by the likely season-ending knee injury to EDGE Aidan Hutchinson, the Lions’ star pass-rusher.

Hutchinson suffered the injury while celebrating a first-quarter sack of Patriots signal-caller Drake Maye; he leaped in the air and upon coming down, landed awkwardly on his right leg. The fifth-year defender never played another snap Sunday.

If that was not a clear-cut sign to cut the acrobatics out of his celebration repertoire, I don't know what would be. Nonetheless, he needs to – no ifs, ands, or buts about it.

The University of Michigan product will receive further testing upon returning home to the states. However, his 2026 campaign is believed to be over, cutting short what had been an All-Pro-caliber season.

His sack of Maye was his seventh on the season, and he also logged another two pressures in the international affair, bringing his season total to 52 (the second-highest total in the NFL).

He easily was one of the league's most productive pass-rushers in 2026, earning a league-leading Pro Football Focus pass-rush grade of 91.1 and an overall mark of 91.9 through nine games (the best overall grade among 111 qualified EDGEs).

Plain and simple, Detroit does not possess another EDGE defender in the same stratosphere as the 2022 No. 2 overall pick. Derrick Moore and DJ Wonnum have each had their moments of looking like competent pass-rushers. However, neither of them is going to be confused for Hutchinson anytime soon.

The Michigan native has become an irreplaceable talent; consequently, losing him for the year is undoubtedly a detrimental blow to Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's unit. Without the premier quarterback disruptor, it certainly is harder to envision Detroit capturing the NFC North crown and making a Super Bowl run.

It begs the question: Should Lions head man Dan Campbell mandate that his players are no longer allowed to leave their feet to celebrate big plays? If I were Campbell, I would do just that.

And no, I'm not trying to take the fun out of the game. I'm fully aware that players like Hutchinson are also entertainers and that they have a genuine passion and love for playing the game. So, I would never want to take away their ability to enjoy themselves while they put their bodies on the line 17 weeks a year. That would be a bad look for Campbell, too, and likely cause him to lose the respect of his players.

It's why the celebrations can and should remain. However, they need to be toned down. And specifically, I'm talking about eliminating the acrobatics, and in the process, reducing the likelihood of another Lions player suffering a season-ending ailment while celebrating a major play.

And Campbell can't sugarcoat the importance of this being the new celebration policy, either. He needs to be steadfast with it and emphasize there is no wiggle room for a Hutchinson 2.0. The NFC North is too good and deep, with the Bears continuing to rack up wins and Kirk Cousins now under center for the Vikings, for the Lions to endure another celebration gone wrong.

The Buffalo Bills are running through opposing quarterback depth charts almost as quickly as they're running through opponents.

Kyle McCord is next.

Buffalo will face its sixth backup quarterback in four games when the former Syracuse star makes his second career start for the Miami Dolphins on Sunday at Highmark Stadium.

Miami placed starting quarterback Malik Willis on injured reserve last week with a groin injury, opening the door for McCord to make his NFL debut against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday.

Bills defense has feasted on backup quarterbacks

The revolving door began Nov. 1 when Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson injured his throwing thumb on the first offensive snap of the game.

Backup Tyler Huntley suffered a toe injury in the second quarter, thrusting undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano into his first NFL game.

Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray missed the following week's game with a hamstring injury. Carson Wentz started and posted an 8.9 passer rating before being replaced by Max Brosmer in the fourth quarter.

New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith exited twice against Buffalo on Sunday, first to be evaluated for a concussion and then with an ankle injury. Fourth-round rookie Cade Klubnik made his NFL debut in relief.

Here's how the five backup quarterbacks have fared against Buffalo:

Tyler Huntley, Ravens: 2-for-4, 0 yards

Joe Fagnano, Ravens: 10-for-21, 91 yards, INT

Carson Wentz, Vikings: 8-for-25, 81 yards, 2 INTs

Max Brosmer, Vikings: 6-for-7, 58 yards

Cade Klubnik, Jets: 11-for-20, 137 yards, INT

That's a combined 48.1% completion percentage, 367 passing yards, zero touchdowns, four interceptions and a 41.4 passer rating.

Buffalo has outscored its opponents 90-28 during that stretch.

Kyle McCord sets Dolphins record in NFL debut

McCord made franchise history in his first NFL game despite Miami's 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.

He completed 17 of 32 passes for 209 yards, the most passing yards by a Dolphins quarterback in his NFL debut.

McCord didn't throw a touchdown pass or an interception but ran for a touchdown and lost a fumble in his own end zone that Indianapolis recovered for a touchdown.

Miami nearly overcame a 21-7 second-half deficit despite kicker Zane Gonzalez missing two field goals and an extra point.

Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley was encouraged by McCord's demeanor.

“He was composed, he didn't get rattled,” Hafley said.

McCord, 24, spent three seasons at Ohio State before transferring to Syracuse, where he put together one of the most prolific passing seasons in ACC history.

He led the nation with 4,779 passing yards in 2024, setting an ACC single-season record, and threw 34 touchdown passes while leading the Orange to a 10-3 record.

The Philadelphia Eagles selected McCord in the sixth round of the 2025 NFL Draft and he spent his rookie season on their practice squad.

He signed with the Green Bay Packers in January and completed 46 of 70 passes for 446 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions in three preseason games. Green Bay traded him to Miami for a 2028 sixth-round draft pick in August.

His second career start will bring him back to upstate New York to face a defense that hasn't surrendered a touchdown since the first quarter of November.

text:
Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson will miss the rest of the NFL season after sustaining a serious knee injury while celebrating.

Hutchinson, 26, jumped in the air after bringing down New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye in the first quarter of the Lions' 35-10 win in Munich.

The 2022 second overall pick fell to the ground shortly after landing, clutching his right knee.

Hutchinson walked to the sideline after medical treatment on the field but did not return to the game - and has torn his anterior cruciate ligament.

It is the second season-ending injury of Hutchinson career - but Lions head coach Dan Campbell has no plans to stop his players from expressing themselves.

"I hate it. I think we all understand what it is, and let's be smart, but no, I'm not gonna say 'nobody celebrates any more'," Campbell said.

"The number of moves that I've seen 'Hutch' make and the number of plyometrics, explosive movements, the spins, the one-leg lateral movements, lateral balances... it was one of those things, man."

This was the sixth regular-season NFL game to be played in Germany and the third to be held at Bayern Munich's Allianz Arena.

The Lions' win means they are top of the NFC North and have the second-best record in the conference.

Hutchinson is regarded as one of the premier pass rushers in the NFL, and is currently tied for 13th in the league with six sacks this season.

Campbell is confident Hutchinson will come back stronger on his return from the injury setback.

"He's such a phenomenal player, an impact player, but more importantly he's an unbelievable team-mate and he's one of our captains," Campbell added.

"What a hell of a year he was having. He's just improved every year and to come off the injury he had [in 2024].

"This guy will overcome this and he will come back better than he was. It's just the way he is, it's the way he's wired."

Drake Maye, Brock Bowers and Aidan Hutchinson injury updates
